China is accused of training AI on American AI Anthropic says operators linked to Alibaba's Qwen team used nearly 25,000 fake accounts to hold over 28 million conversations with Claude, collecting its answers to improve competing models. The technique is called distillation. But getting Claude's answers doesn't mean copying Claude. You still need your own model, engineers, chips, and massive compute. It can help someone catch up faster, but it doesn't explain China's entire AI progress. Distillation itself is legal and widely used. The controversy is doing it without permission. So the real question: if the best AI can be turned into a teacher just by asking enough questions, how long can any lab keep its edge? Share this with someone following the AI race. Reuters reports ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent have ordered more than 3 million Nvidia RTX Pro 5500 chips, about $35 billion, and Nvidia says it can’t guarantee it can fill them. Theo’s take: one source says partners may get only 5 to 10% of what they asked for, and the scale shows how much China still wants Nvidia. How much sway does Jensen have over US chip policy? “ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent have ordered more than three million Nvidia chips, RTX Pro 5500 workstation GPUs, for a total of about $35 billion.” “Nvidia said it can’t guarantee that it can fill the orders because demand exceeds planned production. One source said Nvidia told partners they might receive only 5 to 10% of the quantities requested.” “Total orders from customers in China have exceeded 6 million. So if it’s 6 million, then it’s probably $70 billion between all of China.” “The scale of the orders underscores the ongoing appetite among Chinese companies for Nvidia hardware despite the US curbs. It’s kind of incredible how powerful Jensen is politically.” #tech #techtok #ai #politics #stocks
